sentences.zh: 王奐

translations.literal: Wang Huan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan

sentences.zh: 王奐字彥孫，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Huan, style name Yansun, was a native of Linyi in Langya Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, courtesy name Yansun, came from Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 祖僧朗，宋左光祿、儀同。

translations.literal: His grandfather Senglang was Left Household Grandee and Peer of Three Offices under the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Senglang had served the Song as Left Household Grandee with the privilege of Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 父粹，黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Cui was a Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Cui had been a Yellow Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 奐出繼從祖中書令球，故字彥孫。

translations.literal: Huan was given in adoption to his father's younger cousin, the Secretariat Director Qiu, and therefore took the style name Yansun.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was adopted by his father's cousin, Secretariat Director Wang Qiu, which is why his courtesy name was Yansun.

sentences.zh: 解褐著作佐郎，太子舍人，安陸王冠軍主簿，太子洗馬，本州別駕，中書郎，桂陽王司空諮議，黃門郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the ranks he became Assistant in the Masters of Writing, Crown Prince Attendant, chief clerk to the Champion General of Prince Anlu, Crown Prince Groom, provincial aide of his native commandery, Secretariat Gentleman, staff adviser to the Minister of Works for Prince Guiyang, and Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an assistant in the Masters of Writing, then served successively as crown prince attendant, chief clerk on Prince Anlu's staff, crown prince groom, native commandery aide, secretariat gentleman, adviser to Prince Guiyang's ministry of works, and yellow gate gentleman.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，爲晉熙王征虜長史、江夏內史，遷侍中，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui he became chief administrator to the Expelling Barbarians General for Prince Jinxi and Interior Governor of Jiangxia, then was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In 473 he was made chief administrator on Prince Jinxi's staff and interior governor of Jiangxia, then promoted to palace attendant while also holding the post of colonel of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 復出爲晉熙王鎮西長史，加冠軍將軍、江夏武昌太守。

translations.literal: He was again sent out as chief administrator to the Pacifier of the West for Prince Jinxi, with the additional titles of Champion General and Grand Administrator of Jiangxia and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out again as chief administrator on Prince Jinxi's western staff, with the added rank of champion general and concurrent governorship of Jiangxia and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 徵祠部尚書，轉掌吏部。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Rites and then transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to be minister of rites and soon took charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，遷冠軍將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was transferred to Champion General and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shengming era he was made champion general and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初，王晏父普曜爲沈攸之長史，常慮攸之舉事，不得還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yan's father Puyao had been chief administrator to Shen Youzhi and constantly feared that Youzhi would raise troops and that he would not be able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Yan's father Puyao had served as Shen Youzhi's chief administrator and lived in constant fear that Youzhi would rebel and he would never get home.

sentences.zh: 時奐爲吏部，轉普曜爲內職，晏深德之。

translations.literal: At that time Huan was in the Ministry of Personnel and transferred Puyao to an inner-office post; Yan was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan headed the Ministry of Personnel, he moved Puyao to a court post inside the capital, for which Yan was profoundly grateful.

sentences.zh: 及晏仕世祖府，奐從弟蘊反，世祖謂晏曰：「王奐宋家外戚，王蘊親同逆黨，旣其羣從，豈能無異意。

translations.literal: When Yan entered service in the Heir Apparent's establishment, Huan's younger cousin Yun rebelled. The Heir Apparent said to Yan: "Wang Huan is a Song-dynasty affinal kinsman; Wang Yun is a close associate of the rebel faction. Since they are of the same clan, how can they lack ulterior motives?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan joined the heir apparent's staff, Huan's cousin Wang Yun rose in revolt. The heir apparent told Yan, "Wang Huan is tied to the Song by marriage, and Wang Yun stands with the rebels. Men of the same clan—how can they be free of divided loyalties?"

sentences.zh: 我欲具以啓聞。

translations.literal: I wish to report the full matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to lay the whole matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 」晏叩頭曰：「王奐脩謹，保無異志。

translations.literal: " Yan kowtowed and said: "Wang Huan is cultivated and cautious; I guarantee he harbors no disloyal intent."
translations.idiomatic: " Yan kowtowed and said, "Wang Huan is scrupulous and careful—I swear he has no treacherous designs."

sentences.zh: 晏父母在都，請以爲質。

translations.literal: Yan's parents are in the capital; I ask that they be held as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: My parents are in the capital—let them stand as hostages for him."

sentences.zh: 」世祖乃止。

translations.literal: " The Heir Apparent then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The heir apparent dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 出爲吳興太守，秩中二千石，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Wuxing, with salary at the two-thousand-dan middle grade, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to govern Wuxing at the middle two-thousand-dan rank, retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 尋進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to Expelling Barbarians General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his title was raised to expelling barbarians general.

sentences.zh: ，進號左將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was advanced to Left General.
translations.idiomatic: In 479 he was promoted to left general.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷太常，領鄱陽王師，仍轉侍中，祕書監，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Grand Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently Tutor to Prince Poyang, then turned to Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became grand minister of ceremonies and tutor to Prince Poyang, then palace attendant, director of the secretariat, and valiant cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 又遷征虜將軍、臨川王鎮西長史、領南蠻校尉、南郡內史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Expelling Barbarians General, chief administrator to the Pacifier of the West for Prince Linchuan, and concurrently Colonel of Southern Man and Interior Governor of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved again to expelling barbarians general, chief administrator on Prince Linchuan's western staff, with the added posts of colonel of the southern barbarians and interior governor of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 奐一歲三遷，上表固讓南蠻曰：「今天地初辟，萬物載新，荊蠻來威，巴濮不擾。

translations.literal: Huan was promoted three times in one year. He submitted a memorial firmly declining the post of Colonel of Southern Man, saying: "Now heaven and earth have just been opened anew and the ten thousand things are laden with freshness; the Jing barbarians have come to show their awe, and Ba and Pu are undisturbed."
translations.idiomatic: Huan received three promotions within a single year. He memorialized the throne, firmly declining the southern barbarians command, writing: "Heaven and earth have only just been renewed; all things are fresh again. The tribes of Jing have submitted, and Ba and Pu are quiet."

sentences.zh: 但使邊民樂業，有司脩務，本府舊州，日就殷阜。

translations.literal: If only the border people are made content in their occupations and the responsible offices attend to their duties, this former province of the headquarters will daily grow prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Let the frontier people prosper in their work and the officials do theirs, and this old seat of government will grow richer day by day.

sentences.zh: 臣昔遊西土，較見盈虛，兼日者戎燼之後，痍毀難復。

translations.literal: Your servant once traveled in the western lands and has closely observed their fullness and emptiness; moreover, since the recent aftermath of war's embers, wounds and ruin are hard to restore.
translations.idiomatic: I have traveled in the west before and seen firsthand how lean or full those regions are; and since the recent wars, the devastation has been so deep that recovery is still far off.

sentences.zh: 雖復緝以善政，未及來蘇。

translations.literal: Even if good government is again applied, it has not yet reached the point of returning to life.
translations.idiomatic: Even the best governance has not yet brought those lands back to life.

sentences.zh: 今復割撤大府，制置偏校，崇望不足以助強，語實安能以相弊？

translations.literal: Now to cut away and withdraw the great headquarters and set up a subordinate command—elevated prestige is insufficient to strengthen it, and in truth how can words make it mutually harmful?
translations.idiomatic: To split off part of the great headquarters and set up a subsidiary command would add prestige without real strength, and in practice can only weaken what is already there.

sentences.zh: 且資力旣分，職司增廣，衆勞務倍，文案滋煩。

translations.literal: Moreover, once resources and strength are divided, offices and duties increase and broaden, the people's labors and tasks are doubled, and paperwork grows ever more troublesome.
translations.idiomatic: Resources would be divided, offices multiplied, public labor doubled, and paperwork endlessly increased.

sentences.zh: 非獨臣見其難，竊以爲國計非允。

translations.literal: It is not only that your servant sees the difficulty; I privately consider the state's plan inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: I am not alone in seeing the difficulty; I believe the policy itself is unsound for the realm.

sentences.zh: 」見許。

translations.literal: " His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 於是罷南蠻校尉官。

translations.literal: Thereupon the office of Colonel of Southern Man was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The post of colonel of the southern barbarians was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 進號前將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vanguard General.
translations.idiomatic: His title was raised to vanguard general.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，徵右僕射。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, Huan was summoned as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Huan was recalled as right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仍轉使持節監湘州軍事、前將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then transferred as bearer of the staff with discretionary authority to oversee Xiang Province military affairs, Vanguard General, and Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made inspector of Xiang with discretionary authority, holding the rank of vanguard general.

sentences.zh: ，徙爲散騎常侍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In 484 he was moved to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and inspector of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 初省江州軍府。

translations.literal: For the first time the Jiang Province military headquarters was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: It was the first reduction of the Jiang province military staff.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷右僕射，本州中正。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of Selection for his native province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongming he became right vice director of the secretariat and director of selection for his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 奐無學術，以事幹見處。

translations.literal: Huan had no scholarly learning and was placed in office for his practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was no scholar; he rose through executive talent.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射，中正如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, his directorship of selection unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the masters of writing while keeping his selection post.

sentences.zh: 校籍郎王植屬吏部郎孔琇之以校籍令史俞公喜求進署，矯稱奐意，植坐免官。

translations.literal: The Registrar of Household Registers Wang Zhi, subordinate to the Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Kong Xiuzhi, had the registrar clerk Yu Gongxi seek advancement in appointment, falsely claiming Huan's approval; Zhi was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Wang Zhi, working under personnel officer Kong Xiuzhi, had clerk Yu Gongxi lobby for promotion in Huan's name without authorization; Zhi was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷散騎常侍，領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general of the guards.

sentences.zh: 奐欲請車駕幸府。

translations.literal: Huan wished to request that the imperial carriage visit his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Huan wanted to invite the emperor to visit his household.

sentences.zh: 上晚信佛法，御膳不宰牲。

translations.literal: The Emperor in his later years believed in Buddhism; the imperial meals did not slaughter animals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had lately taken up Buddhism and would not have animals killed for his table.

sentences.zh: 使王晏謂奐曰：「吾前去年爲斷殺事，不復幸詣大臣已判，無容欻爾也。

translations.literal: He had Wang Yan tell Huan: "I previously, last year, for the matter of ending slaughter, no longer visit ministers' homes—that has been decided; there is no room for such a sudden change."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Yan to tell Huan, "Since I swore off slaughter last year I no longer visit ministers at home—that is settled, and there is no changing it on a whim."

sentences.zh: 」王儉卒，上用奐爲尚書令，以問王晏。

translations.literal: " When Wang Jian died, the Emperor intended to use Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and consulted Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wang Jian died, the emperor meant to make Huan director of the masters of writing and asked Wang Yan's view.

sentences.zh: 晏位遇已重，與奐不能相推，答上曰：「柳世隆有重望，恐不宜在奐後。

translations.literal: Yan's position and favor were already weighty, and he and Huan could not defer to each other. He answered the Emperor: "Liu Shilong enjoys great prestige; I fear it would not be fitting to place him after Huan."
translations.idiomatic: Yan was already too powerful to yield to Huan, and told the emperor, "Liu Shilong's standing is too great—he should not rank below Huan."

sentences.zh: 」乃轉爲左僕射，加給事中，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、鎮北將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: " Huan was therefore transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the additional post of Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, and sent out as bearer of the staff with discretionary authority, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of military affairs for Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, Pacifier of the North General, and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan was made left vice director with the added title of attendant within the yellow gates, then sent out to Yong as inspector with discretionary authority, commanding the armies of Yong, Liang, and northern and southern Qin, with Jingling and Suixiang, under the title pacifier of the north.

sentences.zh: 上謂王晏曰：「奐於釋氏，實自專至。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Wang Yan: "In matters of the Buddhist teaching Huan is in truth utterly devoted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wang Yan, "Huan's devotion to Buddhism is absolute."

sentences.zh: 其在鎮或以此妨務，卿相見言次及之，勿道吾意也。

translations.literal: In the province this may hinder his duties; when you meet, mention it in passing, but do not say it is my intent."
translations.idiomatic: That may interfere with his duties in the province—bring it up casually when you see him, but do not say I sent you."

sentences.zh: 」上以行北諸戍士卒多襤縷，送褶三千具，令奐分賦之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, because the garrison troops on the northern marches were mostly in rags, sent three thousand sets of trousers and had Huan distribute them.
translations.idiomatic: " Learning that the northern garrisons were in rags, the emperor sent three thousand pairs of trousers for Huan to distribute.

sentences.zh: 十一年，奐輙殺寧蠻長史劉興祖，上大怒，使御史中丞孔稚珪奏其事曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Huan on his own authority killed the Pacifier of the Man Chief Administrator Liu Xingzu. The Emperor was greatly enraged and had the Imperial Censor Kong Zhigui memorialize the matter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Huan killed Pacifier of the Man chief administrator Liu Xingzu on his own authority. The emperor was furious and ordered imperial censor Kong Zhigui to present the case:

sentences.zh: :　　雍州刺史王奐啓錄小府長史劉興祖，虛稱「興祖扇動山蠻，規生逆謀，誑言誹謗，言辭不遜」。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yong Province Wang Huan reported and arrested the minor headquarters chief administrator Liu Xingzu, falsely claiming: "Xingzu incites the mountain barbarians, plots rebellion, speaks deceitful slander, and his words are insubordinate."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, inspector of Yong, reported and seized his minor headquarters chief Liu Xingzu, falsely charging that Xingzu was stirring up the mountain tribes, plotting rebellion, spreading slander, and speaking insolently.

sentences.zh: 敕使送興祖下都，奐慮所啓欺妄，於獄打殺興祖，詐啓稱自經死。

translations.literal: An imperial order directed that Xingzu be sent down to the capital. Huan, fearing that his report was deceitful, beat Xingzu to death in prison and falsely reported that he had hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Xingzu sent to the capital. Fearful that his charges would be exposed, Huan had him beaten to death in prison and reported a suicide.

sentences.zh: 止今體傷楗蒼，事暴聞聽。

translations.literal: Only now are the wounds on the body stiff and dark; the affair has burst upon the court's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: The body's wounds are now plain for all to see, and the matter has come openly before the court.

sentences.zh: :　　攝興祖門生劉倪到臺辨問，列「興祖與奐共事，不能相和。

translations.literal: Xingzu's student Liu Ni was taken to the capital for examination and stated: "Xingzu and Huan served together but could not get along."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu's student Liu Ni was brought to the capital for questioning and testified that Xingzu and Huan had served together but never got along.

sentences.zh: 自去年朱公恩領軍征蠻失利，興祖啓聞，以啓呈奐，奐因此便相嫌恨。

translations.literal: Since last year Zhu Gong'en led the army in a campaign against the Man that failed; Xingzu reported this and presented the report to Huan, and Huan therefore came to bear hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Zhu Gong'en's campaign against the Man tribes failed; Xingzu reported it and showed Huan the memorial, after which Huan turned against him.

sentences.zh: 若云興祖有罪，便應事在民間；

translations.literal: If one says Xingzu was guilty, the matter ought to have been among the people;
translations.idiomatic: If Xingzu were truly guilty, the matter should have shown among the people;

sentences.zh: 民間恬然，都無事迹。

translations.literal: among the people all was tranquil and there were no facts at all.
translations.idiomatic: yet the countryside was quiet and no evidence existed.

sentences.zh: 去十年九月十八日，奐使仗身三十人來，稱敕錄興祖付獄。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month of the tenth year past, Huan sent thirty armed attendants, claiming an imperial order to arrest Xingzu and hand him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month, ten years ago, Huan sent thirty armed retainers claiming an imperial order to seize Xingzu and imprison him.

sentences.zh: 安定郡蠻先在郡贓私，興祖旣知其取與，卽牒啓，奐不問。

translations.literal: A barbarian of Anding Commandery had earlier engaged in illicit gain in the commandery; Xingzu, having learned of his taking and giving, immediately submitted a written report, but Huan did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: A tribesman of Anding had been taking bribes in the prefecture; Xingzu learned of it and filed a report, but Huan ignored it.

sentences.zh: 興祖後執錄，奐仍令蠻領仗身於獄守視。

translations.literal: After Xingzu was later arrested, Huan still had the barbarian lead armed attendants to guard and watch him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzu was arrested, Huan even put that tribesman in charge of the guards watching him in prison.

sentences.zh: 興祖未死之前，於獄以物畫漆柈子中出密報家，道無罪，令啓乞出都一辨，萬死無恨」。

translations.literal: Before Xingzu died, in prison he used an object to scratch a secret message inside a lacquered tray and sent it to his family, saying he was guiltless and asking them to memorialize begging to come to the capital for one examination—he would have no regret even in ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Before he died, Xingzu scratched a secret message inside a lacquered tray smuggled to his family, declaring his innocence and begging them to petition for a hearing in the capital—even death would be worth it."

sentences.zh: 又云：「奐駐興祖嚴禁信使，欲作方便，殺以除口舌。

translations.literal: It was also stated: "Huan detained Xingzu with strict prohibition of messengers, wishing to find an opportunity to kill him and remove a voice."
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Huan held Xingzu under strict guard, blocking all messengers, seeking a chance to kill him and silence him.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「奐意乃可。

translations.literal: " It was also stated: "Huan's intent was acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: " He added that Huan's intentions were clear.

sentences.zh: 奐第三息彪隨奐在州，凡事是非皆干豫，扇構密除興祖。

translations.literal: Huan's third son Biao followed Huan in the province; in every matter of right and wrong he intervened, inciting and plotting in secret to remove Xingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's third son Biao was with him in the province, meddling in every decision and secretly plotting Xingzu's removal.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「興祖家餉糜，中下藥，食兩口便覺，回乞獄子，食者皆大利。

translations.literal: " It was also stated: "Xingzu's family sent porridge; drugs were placed in it; after two mouthfuls he felt ill and turned to beg the prison attendants; all who ate suffered severe diarrhea."
translations.idiomatic: " His family sent porridge laced with poison; after two bites Xingzu was ill, and every prisoner who ate it was violently purged."

sentences.zh: 興祖大呌道『糜中有藥』。

translations.literal: Xingzu cried out loudly: "There is poison in the porridge!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu shouted, "The porridge is poisoned!"

sentences.zh: 近獄之家，無人不聞。

translations.literal: Among the households near the prison, there was none who did not hear.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone near the prison heard it.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「奐治著興祖日急，判無濟理。

translations.literal: " It was also stated: "Huan's handling of Xingzu grew daily more urgent; clearly there was no hope of remedy."
translations.idiomatic: " He said Huan's pressure on Xingzu grew daily and there was no hope of saving him."

sentences.zh: 十一月二十一日，奐使獄吏來報興祖家，道興祖於獄自經死。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month Huan sent prison clerks to report to Xingzu's family, saying Xingzu had hanged himself in prison.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the eleventh month Huan's jailers told Xingzu's family he had hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 尸出，家人共洗浴之，見興祖頸下有傷，肩胛烏，陰下破碎，實非興祖自經死。

translations.literal: When the corpse was brought out the family together washed the body and saw wounds beneath Xingzu's neck, blackened shoulder blades, and shattered lower parts—in truth it was not that Xingzu had hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the body was released the family washed it and found wounds on the neck, bruised shoulders, and shattered lower body—clearly not a hanging.

sentences.zh: 家人及門義共見，非是一人。

translations.literal: Family and gate retainers all saw it; it was not a single person.
translations.idiomatic: Family and retainers alike witnessed it—many people, not one.

sentences.zh: 」重攝檢雍州都留田文喜，列與倪符同狀。

translations.literal: " Tian Wenxi, who remained at the Yong headquarters, was again taken for examination; his statements matched Ni's in every particular.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian Wenxi of the Yong headquarters was questioned again and corroborated Ni's account in full.

sentences.zh: :　　興祖在獄，嗛苦望下，旣蒙降旨，欣願始遂，豈容於此，方復自經？

translations.literal: Xingzu in prison had suffered bitterly, looking down for imperial grace; having received the lowered decree, his joyful wish was just fulfilled—how could he at this point hang himself again?
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu had suffered in prison, longing for the capital; once the order came to send him down his hope was fulfilled—how could he then kill himself?

sentences.zh: 敕以十九日至，興祖以二十一日死，推理檢迹，灼然矯假。

translations.literal: The decree was to arrive on the nineteenth; Xingzu died on the twenty-first—reasoning through the evidence, the forgery is glaringly clear.
translations.idiomatic: The decree was due on the nineteenth; Xingzu died on the twenty-first—the timeline alone proves the fraud.

sentences.zh: 尋敕使送下，奐輙拒詔，所謗諸條，悉出奐意。

translations.literal: Soon the imperial messenger was to escort him down; Huan on his own authority refused the decree. Every item of slander issued entirely from Huan's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial escort was sent, Huan defied the order on his own authority; every charge came from his own mind.

sentences.zh: 毀故丞相若陳顯達，誹訕朝事，莫此之深。

translations.literal: He slandered the late Chancellor, as Chen Xianda, and maligned court affairs—nothing deeper than this.
translations.idiomatic: He defamed the late chancellor Chen Xianda and reviled the court—nothing went deeper.

sentences.zh: 彪私隨父之鎮，敢亂王法，罪竝合窮戮。

translations.literal: Biao on his own followed his father to the province and dared to disturb royal law; his crime together merits execution to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had followed his father to the province and dared violate the law—his crimes warrant the fullest punishment.

sentences.zh: 上遣中書舍人呂文顯、直閤將軍曹道剛領齋仗五百人收奐。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Palace Gentleman Lü Wenxian and Direct Gate General Cao Daogang leading five hundred palace guards to take Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace gentleman Lü Wenxian and direct gate general Cao Daogang with five hundred guards to arrest Huan.

sentences.zh: 敕鎮西司馬曹虎從江陵步道會襄陽。

translations.literal: An order directed Pacifier of the West Major Cao Hu to march from Jiangling by the land route and join at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu, major of the western command, was ordered to march from Jiangling overland to join them at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 奐子彪素凶剽，奐不能制。

translations.literal: Huan's son Biao was by nature fierce and violent; Huan could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's son Biao had always been brutal, and Huan could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 女婿殷叡懼禍，謂奐曰：「曹、呂今來，旣不見真敕，恐爲姦變，政宜錄取，馳啓聞耳。

translations.literal: His son-in-law Yin Rui, fearing disaster, said to Huan: "Cao and Lü have now come; since we have not seen the true decree, we fear a treacherous turn of events—it is fitting to arrest them and swiftly memorialize the throne."
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Yin Rui, fearing disaster, urged Huan: "Cao and Lü are here without showing a genuine decree—they may be plotting treachery. Arrest them and report to the throne at once."

sentences.zh: 」奐納之。

translations.literal: " Huan accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan agreed.

sentences.zh: 彪輙令率州內得千餘人，開鎮庫，取仗，配衣甲，出南堂陳兵，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Biao on his own authority ordered that more than a thousand men be mustered within the province, the headquarters arsenal opened, weapons taken, armor issued, troops arrayed in the southern hall, and the gates closed to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: Biao on his own authority rallied more than a thousand men in the province, opened the arsenal, armed them, drew them up in the southern hall, and shut the gates to resist.

sentences.zh: 奐門生鄭羽叩頭啓奐，乞出城迎臺使。

translations.literal: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and reported to Huan, begging to go out of the city to welcome the capital envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and begged permission to go out and receive the imperial envoys.

sentences.zh: 奐曰：「我不作賊，欲先遣啓自申。

translations.literal: Huan said: "I am not making rebellion; I wish first to send a memorial explaining myself."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "I am no rebel—I mean to send a memorial explaining myself first."

sentences.zh: 政恐曹、呂輩小人相陵藉，故且閉門自守耳。

translations.literal: I only fear that petty men like Cao and Lü will bully and insult us, and therefore for the moment close the gates and hold ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear men like Cao and Lü will abuse us, so for now we hold the gates."

sentences.zh: 」彪遂出與虎軍戰，其黨范虎領二百人降臺軍，彪敗走歸。

translations.literal: " Biao then went out to fight Hu's army; his partisan Fan Hu led two hundred men in surrender to the capital army, and Biao was defeated and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: " Biao went out to fight Hu's troops; his follower Fan Hu defected with two hundred men, and Biao was beaten back inside.

sentences.zh: 土人起義攻州西門，彪登門拒戰，却之。

translations.literal: Local people rose in righteous action and attacked the western gate of the province; Biao mounted the gate to resist and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Local militia rose and attacked the western gate; Biao fought them off from the wall.

sentences.zh: 奐司馬黃瑤起、寧蠻長史裴叔業於城內起兵攻奐。

translations.literal: Huan's Major Huang Yaoqi and Pacifier of the Man Chief Administrator Pei Shuye raised troops within the city to attack Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's major Huang Yaoqi and Pacifier of the Man chief Pei Shuye rose inside the city against him.

sentences.zh: 奐聞兵入，還內禮佛，未及起，軍人遂斬之。

translations.literal: Huan, hearing troops enter, returned inside to worship the Buddha; before he could rise, the soldiers beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing soldiers enter, Huan went inside to pray before the Buddha; before he could rise, they cut him down.

sentences.zh: 年五十九。

translations.literal: He was fifty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 執彪及弟爽、弼、殷叡，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Biao and his brothers Shuang and Bi and Yin Rui were seized; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, his brothers Shuang and Bi, and Yin Rui were seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「逆賊王奐，險詖之性，自少及長。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The rebel Wang Huan, of a treacherous and perverse nature from youth to age."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The traitor Wang Huan was treacherous and perverse from youth to old age."

sentences.zh: 外飾廉勤，內懷凶慝，貽戾郷伍，取棄衣冠。

translations.literal: Outwardly he adorned himself with integrity and diligence; inwardly he harbored fierce malice, offending his village and kin and earning rejection by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: He wore the mask of probity while nursing malice within, offending neighbors and forfeiting the respect of the gentry.

sentences.zh: 拔其文筆之用，擢以顯任，出牧樊阿，政刑弛亂。

translations.literal: His literary and clerical talents were drawn forth and he was promoted to conspicuous office; sent out to govern Fan'e, government and punishments were lax and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: His clerical skill won him high office; sent to govern Fan'e, he let law and administration fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 第三息彪矯弄威權，父子均勢。

translations.literal: His third son Biao arrogantly wielded authority; father and son shared equal power.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Biao usurped authority until father and son shared equal power.

sentences.zh: 故寧蠻長史劉興祖忠於奉國，每事匡執，奐忿其異己，誣以訕謗，肆怒囚錄，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: The late Pacifier of the Man Chief Administrator Liu Xingzu was loyal in serving the state and in every matter upheld and corrected; Huan resented his dissent, falsely charged him with slander, in rage imprisoned and arrested him, and only then reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The late Pacifier of the Man chief Liu Xingzu had served the state faithfully and corrected Huan at every turn; Huan, resenting his independence, jailed him on false charges of slander and only then reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朕察奐愚詐，詔送興祖還都，乃懼姦謀發露，潛加殺害。

translations.literal: We perceived Huan's foolish deceit and decreed that Xingzu be sent back to the capital; he then feared his treacherous plot would be exposed and secretly added murder.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing through Huan's deceit, We ordered Xingzu sent to the capital; fearing exposure, he had him killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 欺罔旣彰，中使辯覈，遂授兵登陴，逆捍王命。

translations.literal: Once the deception was manifest and the central envoy examined the case, he then handed out weapons, mounted the ramparts, and in rebellion resisted the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: When the fraud was exposed and the imperial envoy investigated, he armed his men, manned the walls, and defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 天威電掃，義夫咸奮，曾未浹辰，罪人斯獲，方隅克殄，漢南肅清。

translations.literal: Heaven's majesty swept like lightning; righteous men all stirred; before a full day had passed the criminal was taken; the corners of the realm were extinguished; south of the Han was made serene.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial wrath struck like lightning; loyal men rose as one; within a day the culprit was seized, the rebellion crushed, and the lands south of the Han restored to order.

sentences.zh: 自非犯官兼預同逆謀，爲一時所驅逼者，悉無所問。」

translations.literal: Except for guilty officials who also shared in the same rebellious plot, all who were driven and compelled for a time are not to be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Except officials who shared in the plot, all who had been swept along in the moment would go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 奐長子太子中庶子融，融弟司徒從事中郎琛，於都棄市。

translations.literal: Huan's eldest son, Crown Prince Household Aide Rong, and Rong's younger brother, Secretariat Attendant Chen, were exposed in the market at the capital and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's eldest son Rong, crown prince household aide, and his brother Chen, secretariat attendant, were executed in public at the capital.

sentences.zh: 餘孫皆原宥。

translations.literal: The remaining grandsons were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining grandsons were all spared.

translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 殷叡

translations.literal: Yin Rui
translations.idiomatic: Yin Rui

sentences.zh: =殷叡字文子，陳郡人。

translations.literal: Yin Rui, style name Wenzi, was a native of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Rui, courtesy name Wenzi, was from Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉太常融七世孫也。

translations.literal: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Jin Grand Minister of Ceremonies Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was seven generations removed from Jin grand minister of ceremonies Yin Rong.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，祖元素坐染太初事誅。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia under the Song, his grandfather Yuansu was executed for involvement in the Taichu affair.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Song Yuanjia era his grandfather Yuansu was executed for complicity in the Taichu plot.

sentences.zh: 叡遺腹亦當從戮，外曾祖王僧朗啓孝武救之，得免。

translations.literal: Rui, a posthumous child, was also to be put to death with the rest; his great-great-grandfather Wang Senglang memorialized Emperor Xiaowu to save him, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, born after his father's death, was also marked for execution; his great-great-grandfather Wang Senglang pleaded with Emperor Xiaowu and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 叡解文義，有口才，司徒褚淵甚重之，謂之曰：「諸殷自荊州以來，無出卿右者。

translations.literal: Rui understood literary meaning and had eloquence; Minister of Works Chu Yuan greatly valued him and said to him: "Among all the Yin clan since Jing Province, none surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: Rui was literate and articulate; Minister of Works Chu Yuan held him in high regard and said, "Since the Yins came from Jing province, none has matched you."

sentences.zh: 」叡歛容答曰：「殷族衰悴，誠不如昔，若此旨爲虛，故不足降；

translations.literal: " Rui composed his expression and answered: "The Yin clan is in decline and frail, truly not as in former times; if this intent is empty, it is therefore not worth lowering;"
translations.idiomatic: " Rui composed himself and replied, "The Yin clan has declined and is no longer what it was; if you speak in flattery, it is not worth answering;"

sentences.zh: 此旨爲實，彌不可聞。

translations.literal: if this intent is real, it is all the more unbearable to hear.
translations.idiomatic: if you speak in truth, it is all the more unbearable to hear."

sentences.zh: 」奐爲雍州，啓叡爲府長史。

translations.literal: " When Huan was in Yong Province he reported Rui as headquarters chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: " When Huan governed Yong he appointed Rui chief administrator of his staff.

sentences.zh: 叡族父恒，字昭度，與叡同承融後。

translations.literal: Rui's clansman-uncle Heng, style name Zhaodu, with Rui alike inherited from Rong's line.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's kinsman Heng, courtesy name Zhaodu, shared descent from Yin Rong's line with Rui.

sentences.zh: 宋司空景仁孫也。

translations.literal: He was grandson of Song Minister of Works Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: He was grandson of the Song minister of works Yin Jingren.

sentences.zh: 恒及父道矜，竝有古風，以是見蚩於世，其事非一。

translations.literal: Heng and his father Daoqin both had antique manners; on this account they were mocked by the world—their affairs were not few.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and his father Daoqin both cultivated old-fashioned ways and were widely ridiculed for it—there were many such stories.

sentences.zh: 恒，宋泰始初，爲度支尚書，坐屬父疾及身疾多，爲有司所奏。

translations.literal: Heng, at the beginning of Taishi under the Song, was Minister of Revenue; he was impeached because his father's illness and his own frequent illnesses fell under the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Song Taishi era Heng was minister of revenue but was reported for excessive leave due to his father's illness and his own frequent sickness.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔曰：「殷道矜有生便病，比更無橫病。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming decreed: "Yin Daoqin has been ill from birth; recently there has been no sudden illness."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming decreed, "Yin Daoqin has been sick since birth; lately he has had no sudden illness."

sentences.zh: 恒因愚習惰，久妨清敘。

translations.literal: Heng through foolish habit and sloth has long obstructed clear advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's foolish habits and laziness have long blocked his promotion.

sentences.zh: 左遷散騎常侍，領校尉。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Colonel of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and colonel of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 」恒歷官清顯，至金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " Heng held offices that were pure and eminent, reaching Household Grandee with the Golden Bell and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: " Heng served in distinguished posts up to household grandee with golden bell and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 建武中，卒。

translations.literal: During Jianwu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Jianwu era.

sentences.zh: 奐弟女爲長沙王晃妃，世祖詔曰：「奐自陷逆節，長沙王妃男女竝長，且奐又出繼，前代或當有准，可特不離絕。

translations.literal: Huan's younger brother Hui's daughter was consort to Prince Changsha Huang; the Emperor decreed: "Huan has plunged himself into rebellion; the Prince of Changsha's consort and her children are all grown, and moreover Huan was given in adoption—in former ages there may have been precedent; they may specially not be severed."
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Huan's brother Hui was consort to Prince Changsha Huang. The emperor decreed, "Though Huan has rebelled, the princess and her grown children remain, and Huan was adopted out—precedent allows the tie not to be broken."

sentences.zh: 」奐從弟繢。

translations.literal: " Huan's younger cousin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan's cousin Wang Hui.

translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 奐從弟 繢

translations.literal: Huan's younger cousin Hui
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, Huan's cousin

sentences.zh: =繢字叔素，宋車騎將軍景文子也。

translations.literal: Hui, style name Shusu, was son of Song Cavalry General Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, courtesy name Shusu, was the son of Song cavalry general Wang Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，爲祕書郎，太子舍人，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: At twenty he was Secretariat Gentleman, Crown Prince Attendant, then transferred to Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was a secretariat gentleman and crown prince attendant, then palace gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景文以此授超階，令繢經年乃受。

translations.literal: Jingwen for this granted him a leap in rank and had Hui wait a full year before accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen had granted him a leap in rank but made Hui wait a year before accepting it.

sentences.zh: 景文封江安侯，繢襲其本爵，爲始平縣五等男。

translations.literal: Jingwen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an; Hui inherited his original rank as fifth-grade Baron of Shiping County.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen was made Marquis of Jiang'an; Hui inherited his original title as fifth-grade baron of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書丞，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Assistant and Right Chief Administrator of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became secretariat assistant and right chief administrator on the ministry of works staff.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，除寧朔將軍、建平王征北長史、南東海太守，黃門郎，寧朔將軍、東陽太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he was appointed Pacifying the North General, chief administrator to the Northern Expedition for Prince Jianping, Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai, Yellow Gate Gentleman, Pacifying the North General, and Grand Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanhui he was made pacifying the north general, chief administrator on Prince Jianping's northern staff, governor of southern Donghai, yellow gate gentleman, and governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 世祖爲撫軍，吏部尚書張岱選繢爲長史，呈選牒。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent was Pacifying General, Minister of Personnel Zhang Dai selected Hui as chief administrator and presented the selection document.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent held the pacifying general post, personnel minister Zhang Dai nominated Hui as chief administrator and submitted the appointment papers.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑謂岱曰：「此可謂素望。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor smiled and said to Dai: "This may be called longstanding repute."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor smiled and told Dai, "That is what one calls an established reputation."

sentences.zh: 」遷散騎常侍，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and valiant cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 出補義興太守。

translations.literal: He went out to fill the post of Grand Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as governor of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 輙錄郡吏陳伯喜付陽羨獄，欲殺之，縣令孔逭不知何罪，不受繢教，爲有司所奏，繢坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: He on his own authority arrested the commandery clerk Chen Boxi and sent him to Yangxian prison, wishing to kill him; the county magistrate Kong Huan did not know what crime was involved and did not accept Hui's order; he was reported by the responsible offices, and Hui was punished by serving in plain dress while retaining office.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested commandery clerk Chen Boxi and sent him to Yangxian prison to be killed; county magistrate Kong Huan, not knowing the charge, refused the order; reported to the authorities, Hui was reduced to serving in plain clothes while keeping his post.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子，領驍騎，轉長兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Crown Prince Household Aide, concurrently Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became crown prince household aide with valiant cavalry command, then chief concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖出射雉，繢信佛法，稱疾不從駕。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went out to shoot pheasants, Hui believed in Buddhism and claimed illness, not following the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went pheasant hunting, Hui, a devout Buddhist, pleaded illness and stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 轉左民尚書，以母老乞解職，改授寧朔將軍、大司馬長史、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Left for the People; because his mother was old he begged to resign office and was reassigned as Pacifying the North General, chief administrator to the Grand Marshal, and Grand Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of the left for the people, then resigned because his mother was elderly and was reassigned as pacifying the north general, grand marshal chief administrator, and governor of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣城太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Xuancheng, with salary at the two-thousand-dan middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to govern Xuancheng at the middle two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: ，遷輔國將軍、太傅長史，不拜。

translations.literal: In Longchang year 1 he was transferred to Supporter of the State General and chief administrator to the Grand Tutor but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In 494 he was offered supporter of the state general and grand tutor chief administrator but declined.

sentences.zh: 仍爲冠軍將軍、豫章內史。

translations.literal: He was then made Champion General and Interior Governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as champion general and interior governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Expelling Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His title was raised to expelling barbarians general.

sentences.zh: 又坐事免官。

translations.literal: He again was dismissed from office on account of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He was again dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 除冠軍將軍，司徒左長史，散騎常侍，隨王師。

translations.literal: He was appointed Champion General, Left Chief Administrator of the Ministry of Works, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Tutor to Prince Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed champion general, left chief administrator of the ministry of works, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and tutor to Prince Sui.

sentences.zh: 除征虜將軍，驃騎長史，遷散騎常侍，太常。

translations.literal: He was appointed Expelling Barbarians General and chief administrator to the Swift Cavalry, then transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made expelling barbarians general and swift cavalry chief administrator, then cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and grand minister of ceremonies.

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 499 he died.

sentences.zh: 年五十三。

translations.literal: He was fifty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 諡靖子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Jingzi.

sentences.zh: 繢女適安陸王子敬，世祖寵子。

translations.literal: Hui's daughter married Prince Anlu Zijing, the Emperor's favored son.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's daughter married Prince Anlu Zijing, the emperor's favorite son.

sentences.zh: ，納妃，脩外舅姑之敬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming she was received as consort and observed the respect due to parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: In 485 she was installed as consort and showed full respect to her husband's parents by marriage.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣文惠太子相隨往繢家置酒設樂，公卿皆冠冕而至，當世榮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Crown Prince Wenhuì to accompany him in going to Hui's house to set out wine and music; dukes and ministers all came in formal caps and robes—the age counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Crown Prince Wenhuì with him to Hui's home for a feast with music; the highest officials all came in full court dress—a glory of the age.

sentences.zh: 張沖

translations.literal: Zhang Chong
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong

sentences.zh: 張沖字思約，吳郡吳人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, style name Siyue, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, courtesy name Siyue, was from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父柬，通直郎。

translations.literal: His father Jian was a Direct Communication Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Jian was a direct communication gentleman.

sentences.zh: 沖出繼從伯侍中景胤，小名查，父邵，小名梨。

translations.literal: Chong was given in adoption to his father's elder cousin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Jingyin; his childhood name was Cha; his father Shao's childhood name was Li.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was adopted by his father's cousin, attendant-in-ordinary Zhang Jingyin; his childhood name was Cha; his father Shao's was Li.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝戲景胤曰：「查何如梨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song jested with Jingyin: "How does Cha compare with Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song teased Jingyin, "How does Cha compare with Li?"

sentences.zh: 」景胤答曰：「梨是百果之宗，查何敢及。」

translations.literal: " Jingyin answered: "The pear is sovereign among the hundred fruits; how dare Cha compare?"
translations.idiomatic: " Jingyin replied, "The pear is lord of all fruits—how could Cha compare?"

sentences.zh: 沖亦少有至性，辟州主簿，隨從叔永爲將帥，除綏遠將軍、盱眙太守。

translations.literal: Chong also from youth had utmost sincerity; he was summoned as provincial chief clerk, followed his younger cousin Yong as a military commander, and was appointed Pacifying the Distant General and Grand Administrator of Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong too was known from youth for deep filial feeling; summoned as provincial chief clerk, he followed his cousin Yong on campaign and was made pacifying the distant general and governor of Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 永征彭城，遇寒雪，軍人足脛凍斷者十七八，沖足指皆墮。

translations.literal: Yong campaigned against Pengcheng and encountered cold snow; seven or eight out of ten soldiers had calves frozen and broken off; Chong's toes all fell off.
translations.idiomatic: On Yong's Pengcheng campaign they met blizzards; seven or eight soldiers in ten lost feet to frostbite, and Chong lost all his toes.

sentences.zh: 除尚書駕部郎，桂陽王征南中兵，振威將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Master of Writing in the Imperial Transport Section, central army officer on the Southern Expedition for Prince Guiyang, and Inspiring Awe General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made master of writing in the imperial transport section, central army officer on Prince Guiyang's southern staff, and inspiring awe general.

sentences.zh: 歷驃騎太尉南中郎參軍，不拜。

translations.literal: He passed through service as military aide in the Southern Gentlemen's Command of the Swift Cavalry Grand Marshal but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered a post as military aide on the swift cavalry grand marshal's staff but declined.

sentences.zh: 遷征西從事中郎，通直郎，武陵王北中郎直兵參軍，長水校尉，除寧朔將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Expedition Attendant, Direct Communication Gentleman, direct military aide to the Northern Gentlemen's Command for Prince Wuling, Colonel of the Long River, and appointed Pacifying the North General, his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He became western expedition attendant, direct communication gentleman, direct military aide on Prince Wuling's northern staff, colonel of the long river, and pacifying the north general while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 遷左軍將軍，加寧朔將軍，輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Army General, with the additional titles of Pacifying the North General and Supporter of the State General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left army general with the added ranks of pacifying the north and supporter of the state.

sentences.zh: 沖少從戎事，朝廷以幹力相待，故歷處軍校之官。

translations.literal: Chong from youth followed military affairs; the court treated him for his practical ability, and therefore he successively held military and commandery offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had soldiered since youth; the court valued his executive ability and kept him in military posts.

sentences.zh: 出爲馬頭太守，徙盱眙太守，輔國將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Matou, was transferred to Grand Administrator of Xuyi, his Supporter of the State generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Matou, then Xuyi, retaining his supporter of the state rank.

sentences.zh: ，遷西陽王冠軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming he was transferred to Champion Major for Prince Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 488 he became champion major on Prince Xiyang's staff.

sentences.zh: 八年，爲假節、監青冀二州刺史事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he held provisional staff and oversaw the affairs of Qing and Ji provinces, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he held provisional authority over Qing and Ji provinces, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 沖父初卒，遺命曰：「祭我必以郷土所產，無用牲物。

translations.literal: When Chong's father first died, his testament said: "In sacrificing to me you must use what the native place produces; do not use sacrificial animals."
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he left instructions: "Sacrifice to me only with produce of our homeland—no slaughtered animals."

sentences.zh: 」沖在鎮，四時還吳園中取果菜，流涕薦焉。

translations.literal: " While Chong was in the province, in the four seasons he returned to the Wu gardens to take fruits and vegetables and, weeping, offered them.
translations.idiomatic: " While stationed away, each season he returned to the family gardens in Wu for fruit and vegetables and offered them with tears.

sentences.zh: 仍轉刺史。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Chong's title was advanced to Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin ascended, Chong was promoted to champion general.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，以晉壽太守王洪範代沖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Wang Hongfan, Grand Administrator of Jinshou, replaced Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took power, Jinshou governor Wang Hongfan replaced him.

sentences.zh: 除黃門郎，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman with the additional title of Expelling Barbarians General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made yellow gate gentleman with the added rank of expelling barbarians general.

sentences.zh: ，虜寇淮泗，假沖節，都督青冀二州北討諸軍事，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu the barbarians raided Huai and Si; Chong was given provisional staff and made Commander of the Northern Expedition military affairs of Qing and Ji provinces, his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In 495 the enemy raided the Huai and Si region; Chong was given provisional authority to command the northern campaign in Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 虜并兵攻司州，詔青徐出軍分其兵勢。

translations.literal: The barbarians combined forces to attack Si Province; an edict directed Qing and Xu to send out armies to divide their military strength.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy massed against Si province; the court ordered armies from Qing and Xu to divide their strength.

sentences.zh: 沖遣軍主桑係祖由渣口攻拔虜建陵、驛馬、厚丘三城，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: Chong sent the army commander Sang Xizu through Zhakou to storm and take the enemy cities of Jianling, Yima, and Houqiu, with many killed and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent commander Sang Xizu through Zhakou to capture the enemy cities of Jianling, Yima, and Houqiu with heavy slaughter and booty.

sentences.zh: 又與洪範遣軍主崔季延襲虜紀城，據之。

translations.literal: Together with Hongfan he also sent the army commander Cui Jiyan to strike the enemy city of Jicheng and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: With Hongfan he sent commander Cui Jiyan to seize and hold the enemy city of Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 沖又遣軍主杜僧護攻拔虜虎坑、馮時、卽丘三城，驅生口輜重還，至溘溝，虜救兵至，緣道要擊，僧護力戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Chong also sent the army commander Du Senghu to storm and take the enemy cities of Hukeng, Fengshi, and Jiqiu, driving captives and baggage back; at Keigou the enemy relief army arrived and lay in ambush along the road; Senghu fought fiercely and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also sent Du Senghu to take Hukeng, Fengshi, and Jiqiu, driving captives and baggage homeward; at Keigou enemy reinforcements ambushed the road, but Senghu fought them off in a great victory.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷廬陵王北中郎司馬、加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Northern Gentlemen's Major for Prince Luling with the additional title of Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became northern gentlemen's major on Prince Luling's staff with the rank of champion general.

sentences.zh: 未拜，豐城公遙昌爲豫州，上慮寇難未已，徙沖爲征虜長史、南梁郡太守。

translations.literal: Before he accepted, Duke of Fengcheng Yaochang was in Yu Province; the Emperor, fearing that border troubles were not yet ended, transferred Chong to chief administrator to the Expelling Barbarians and Grand Administrator of Nanliang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post, Duke of Fengcheng Yaochang held Yu province; fearing continued border trouble, the emperor moved Chong to expelling barbarians chief administrator and governor of Nanliang.

sentences.zh: ，除江夏王前軍長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was appointed chief administrator to the Vanguard Army for Prince Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In 498 he was made chief administrator on Prince Jiangxia's vanguard staff.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，出爲建安王征虜長史、輔國將軍、江夏內史，行郢州府州事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun took the throne, Chong went out as chief administrator to the Expelling Barbarians for Prince Jian'an, Supporter of the State General, Interior Governor of Jiangxia, and acting head of Jing Province headquarters and province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun ascended, Chong went out as expelling barbarians chief administrator on Prince Jian'an's staff, supporter of the state general, interior governor of Jiangxia, and acting administrator of Jing province.

sentences.zh: ，遷持節、督豫州軍事、豫州刺史，代裴叔業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was transferred as bearer of the staff, Commander of Yu Province military affairs, and Inspector of Yu Province, replacing Pei Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: In 499 he was made inspector of Yu with discretionary authority, replacing Pei Shuye.

sentences.zh: 竟不行。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He never actually took up the post.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷督南兖兖徐青冀五州、輔國將軍、南兖州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred as Commander of the five provinces of Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Supporter of the State General, and Inspector of Southern Yan, his staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made commander of southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, supporter of the state general, and inspector of southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 會司州刺史申希祖卒，以沖爲督司州軍事、冠軍將軍、司州刺史。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Si Province Shen Xizu died, Chong was made Commander of Si Province military affairs, Champion General, and Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Si inspector Shen Xizu died, Chong was appointed to command Si's armies as champion general and inspector.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業以壽春降虜，又遷沖爲督南兖兖徐青冀五州、南兖州刺史，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the barbarians; Chong was again transferred as Commander of the five provinces of Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and Inspector of Southern Yan, his staff and generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the enemy, Chong was again assigned the five provinces and southern Yan, retaining his staff and rank.

sentences.zh: 竝未拜。

translations.literal: None of these was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of these appointments.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景事平，徵建安王寶夤還都，以沖爲督郢司二州、郢州刺史，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing's affair was settled, Prince Jian'an Bao Yin was summoned back to the capital and Chong was made Commander of the two provinces of Jing and Si and Inspector of Jing, his staff and generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's rebellion was crushed, Prince Jian'an was recalled and Chong was made commander of Jing and Si and inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 一歲之中，頻授四州，至此受任。

translations.literal: Within one year he was frequently appointed to four provinces; only now did he accept the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Four provinces had been offered him within a single year; only now did he accept command.

sentences.zh: 其冬，進征虜將軍。

translations.literal: That winter his title was advanced to Expelling Barbarians General.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to expelling barbarians general.

sentences.zh: 封定襄侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 梁王義師起，東昏遣驍騎將軍薛元嗣、制局監暨榮伯領兵及糧運百四十餘船送沖，使拒西師。

translations.literal: When Prince of Liang's righteous army rose, Emperor Donghun sent Valiant Cavalry General Xue Yuansi and Bureau Supervisor Ji Rongbo leading troops and more than a hundred and forty grain-transport ships to reinforce Chong, ordering him to resist the western army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Liang's army rose, Emperor Donghun sent Xue Yuansi and Ji Rongbo with troops and over 140 grain ships to reinforce Chong against the western forces.

sentences.zh: 元嗣等懲劉山陽之敗，疑沖不敢進，停住夏口浦。

translations.literal: Yuansi and the others, mindful of Liu Shanyang's defeat, suspected Chong would not dare advance and halted at Xiakou Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Liu Shanyang's defeat, Yuansi and his men doubted Chong would advance and halted at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 聞義師將至，元嗣、榮伯相率入郢城。

translations.literal: Hearing that the righteous army was about to arrive, Yuansi and Rongbo together led their men into Jing city.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the righteous army was near, Yuansi and Rongbo withdrew into Jing city together.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵太守房僧寄被代還至郢，東昏敕僧寄留守魯山，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Administrator of Jingling, Fang Sengji, having been replaced was returning to Jing; Emperor Donghun ordered Sengji to remain and hold Lushan and appointed him Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Jingling governor Fang Sengji, relieved of office, was returning to Jing; Emperor Donghun ordered him to hold Lushan and made him valiant cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 僧寄謂沖曰：「臣雖未荷朝廷深恩，實蒙先帝厚澤。

translations.literal: Sengji said to Chong: "Your servant has not received the court's deep grace, yet in truth I have enjoyed the former Emperor's generous favor."
translations.idiomatic: Sengji told Chong, "I have not earned the present court's favor, but I owe the late emperor a great debt."

sentences.zh: 蔭其樹者不折其枝，實欲微立塵效。

translations.literal: One who shades the tree does not break its branches; in truth I wish to set up a slight dust-like merit.
translations.idiomatic: One who enjoys the shade does not break the branches—I only wish to render some small service.

sentences.zh: 」沖深相許諾，共結盟誓。

translations.literal: " Chong deeply pledged agreement with him and together they formed a sworn alliance.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong gave his solemn pledge, and they bound themselves by oath.

sentences.zh: 乃分部拒守。

translations.literal: Thereupon they divided their forces to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: They then divided their forces to hold the defenses.

sentences.zh: 遣軍主孫樂祖數千人助僧寄據魯山岸立城壘。

translations.literal: He sent the army commander Sun Lezu with several thousand men to help Sengji hold Lushan, building ramparts on the bank.
translations.idiomatic: He sent commander Sun Lezu with several thousand men to help Sengji fortify Lushan on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，梁王出沔口，圍魯山城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year the Prince of Liang came out from Hankou and besieged Lushan city.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month the Prince of Liang advanced from Hankou and besieged Lushan.

sentences.zh: 遣軍主曹景宗等過江攻郢城，未及盡濟，沖遣中兵參軍陳光靜等開門出擊，爲義師所破，光靜戰死，沖固守不出。

translations.literal: He sent the army commanders Cao Jingzong and others across the river to attack Jing city; before all had crossed, Chong sent the central army aide Chen Guangjing and others to open the gates and strike out; they were defeated by the righteous army, Guangjing died in battle, and Chong held firm without coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzong and others crossed the river against Jing city; before the crossing was complete, Chong sent Chen Guangjing out through the gates in a sortie; the righteous army broke them, Guangjing was killed, and Chong held the city without emerging.

sentences.zh: 景宗於是據石橋浦，連軍相續，下至加湖。

translations.literal: Jingzong thereupon took Shiqiao Ford, linking armies in succession down to Jia Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong then occupied Shiqiao Ford and extended his lines down to Jia Lake.

sentences.zh: 東昏遣軍主巴西梓潼二郡太守吳子陽、光子衿、李文釗、陳虎牙等十三軍援郢，至加湖不得進，乃築城舉烽，城內亦舉火應之。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun sent the army commanders Wu Ziyang, Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong, Guang Zijin, Li Wenzhao, Chen Huya, and thirteen armies to relieve Jing; reaching Jia Lake they could not advance, and therefore built a fort and raised beacon fires; within the city fires were also raised in response.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun sent Wu Ziyang of Baxi and Zitong, Guang Zijin, Li Wenzhao, Chen Huya, and thirteen armies to relieve Jing; halted at Jia Lake, they built a fort and lit beacon fires, answered by signal fires from within the city.

sentences.zh: 而內外各自保，不能相救。

translations.literal: Yet inner and outer each held themselves secure and could not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: But the forces inside and out each held their own ground and could not help one another.

sentences.zh: 沖病死，元嗣、榮伯與沖子孜及長史江夏內史程茂固守。

translations.literal: Chong died of illness; Yuansi, Rongbo, Chong's son Zi, and Chief Administrator and Interior Governor of Jiangxia Cheng Mao held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Chong died of illness; Yuansi, Rongbo, his son Zi, and chief administrator Cheng Mao continued the defense.

sentences.zh: 東昏詔贈沖散騎常侍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun decreed posthumous gifts to Chong of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Protector of the Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun posthumously honored Chong as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 假元嗣子陽節。

translations.literal: Yuansi was given provisional staff as Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi was granted provisional authority under Ziyang's commission.

sentences.zh: 江水暴長，加湖城淹漬，義師乘高艦攻之，子陽等大敗散。

translations.literal: The Yangtze waters swelled violently; Jia Lake city was inundated; the righteous army boarded tall ships to attack; Ziyang and the others were greatly defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze rose in flood and drowned the fort at Jia Lake; the righteous army attacked from high ships and routed Ziyang's forces.

sentences.zh: 魯山城乏糧，軍人於磯頭捕細魚供食，密治輕船，將奔夏口。

translations.literal: Lushan city lacked grain; soldiers at the stony bank caught small fish for food and secretly prepared light boats, intending to flee to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan ran out of grain; soldiers caught small fish at the stony shore and secretly built light boats to escape to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 梁王命偏軍斷其取路，防備越逸。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang ordered detached forces to cut off their escape route and guard against their breaking out.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang sent detachments to block their escape and prevent a breakout.

sentences.zh: 房僧寄病死，孫樂祖窘，以城降。

translations.literal: Fang Sengji died of illness; Sun Lezu, pressed hard, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Sengji died; Sun Lezu, cornered, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 郢城被圍二百餘日，士庶病死者七八百家。

translations.literal: Jing city was besieged for more than two hundred days; among the gentry and common people seven or eight hundred households died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was besieged for over two hundred days; seven or eight hundred households among the populace died of disease.

sentences.zh: 魯山旣敗，程茂及元嗣等議降，使孜爲書與梁王。

translations.literal: After Lushan fell, Cheng Mao and Yuansi and the others discussed surrender and had Zi write a letter to the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan fell, Cheng Mao and Yuansi debated surrender and had Zi write to the Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 沖故吏青州治中房長瑜謂孜曰：「前使君忠貫昊天，操逾松竹。

translations.literal: Chong's former subordinate, Director of Selection for Qing Province Fang Changyu, said to Zi: "The former envoy's loyalty pierced heaven; his conduct surpassed pine and bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: Chong's former officer Fang Changyu, director of selection for Qing, told Zi, "Your father's loyalty reached heaven; his integrity surpassed pine and bamboo."

sentences.zh: 郎君但當端坐畫一，以荷析薪。

translations.literal: The young lord need only sit upright and hold to one course, to bear the burden of splitting firewood.
translations.idiomatic: You need only hold firm to one course and bear the family burden.

sentences.zh: 若天運不與，幅巾待命，以下從使君。

translations.literal: If heaven's fortune is not with you, wait in plain cloth and follow your lord below.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune fails, wait in plain dress to follow your father below.

sentences.zh: 今若隨諸人之計，非唯郢州士女失高山之望，亦恐彼所不取也。

translations.literal: If now you follow the others' plan, not only will the men and women of Jing Province lose their hope set on a high mountain; I also fear they will not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: If you follow the others now, you will disappoint all Jing—and they may not accept you either."

sentences.zh: 」魯山陷後二日，元嗣等以郢城降。

translations.literal: " Two days after Lushan fell, Yuansi and the others surrendered Jing city.
translations.idiomatic: " Two days after Lushan fell, Yuansi surrendered Jing.

sentences.zh: 東昏以程茂爲督郢司二州、輔國將軍、郢州刺史，元嗣爲督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡、冠軍將軍、雍州刺史，竝持節。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun made Cheng Mao Commander of the two provinces of Jing and Si, Supporter of the State General, and Inspector of Jing; Yuansi Commander of Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, Champion General, and Inspector of Yong—both bearing the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun appointed Cheng Mao to command Jing and Si and made Yuansi commander of Yong and the four Qin provinces with Jingling and Suixiang—both with full authority.

sentences.zh: 時郢魯二城已降，死者相積，竟無叛散。

translations.literal: At that time the two cities of Jing and Lu had already surrendered; the dead lay heaped together, yet in the end there was no defection or scattering.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jing and Lushan had fallen with the dead piled high, none had defected or fled.

sentences.zh: 時以沖及房僧寄比臧洪之被圍也。

translations.literal: At the time Chong and Fang Sengji were compared to Zang Hong under siege.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Fang Sengji were then compared to Zang Hong besieged at his post.

sentences.zh: 贈僧寄益州刺史。

translations.literal: Sengji was posthumously given the post of Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sengji was posthumously made inspector of Yi province.

sentences.zh: 時新蔡太守席謙，永明中爲中書郎王融所薦。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Administrator of Xincai, Xi Qian, in Yongming had been recommended by Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Xincai governor Xi Qian had been recommended in the Yongming era by secretariat gentleman Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 父恭穆，鎮西司馬，爲魚復侯所害。

translations.literal: His father Gongmu, Major of the Pacifier of the West, was killed by the Marquis of Yufu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gongmu, major of the western command, was killed by the Marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 至是謙鎮盆城，聞義師東下，曰：「我家世忠貞，殞死不二。

translations.literal: At this time Qian was stationed at Pencheng; hearing the righteous army was coming east, he said: "My family for generations has been loyal and true; we die without a second thought."
translations.idiomatic: Now holding Pencheng, he heard the righteous army was marching east and said, "My family has been loyal for generations—we die without wavering."

sentences.zh: 」爲陳伯之所殺。

translations.literal: " He was killed by Chen Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Bozhi killed him.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: Historian's Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：石碏棄子，弘滅親之戒；

translations.literal: The historian says: Shi Que abandoned his son, spreading the warning against destroying kin;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Shi Que abandoned his son, teaching the warning against destroying one's kin;

sentences.zh: 鮑永晚降，知事新之節。

translations.literal: Bao Yong submitted late, knowing the principle of serving the new.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yong submitted late, yet knew the duty of serving the new order.

sentences.zh: 王奐誠在靡貳，迹允嚴科；

translations.literal: Wang Huan's loyalty was without duplicity, his conduct fitting the severe code;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan was loyal without duplicity, his conduct meeting the harsh standard;

sentences.zh: 張沖未達天心，守迷義運。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong did not comprehend heaven's mind and clung in delusion to righteous fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong failed to read heaven's intent and clung blindly to a doomed cause.

sentences.zh: 致危之理異，爲亡之事一也。

translations.literal: The principles that brought danger differed, but the matter of perishing was one.
translations.idiomatic: The paths to ruin differed, but the end was the same.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王居北牧，子未克家。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wang held the northern pastures; the son could not govern the family.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Wang ruled the north; his son could not keep the house.

sentences.zh: 終成干紀，覆此冑華。

translations.literal: In the end he accomplished rebellion against the statutes and overturned this helmet's glory.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion followed at last, and this house's glory was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 張壘窮守，死如亂麻。

translations.literal: Zhang's fortress was besieged to the end; deaths piled like tangled hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's fortress held to the end; the dead lay tangled like hemp.

sentences.zh: 爲悟旣晚，辯見方賒。

translations.literal: Awakening came too late; clear judgment was still wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Understanding came too late; clear sight was still far off.

sentences.zh: 除青石疑

translations.literal: Removed passages marked as doubtful in blue-green ink.
translations.idiomatic: Removed passages marked as doubtful in blue-green ink.
